A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedLLM survey and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references. Content can be matched despite extensive reorganization. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Although primarily a survey, v1 reports original memory and computational profiling in Sections 3.3–3.4 and Figures 7–8, explicitly described as the authors' experiments and results.

after.justification: v2 retains the authors' memory and FLOPs profiling in Sections 3.3–3.4 and Figures 7–8. Retained original measurements qualify as empirical results.

M1.justification: The surveyed tuning procedures and core taxonomy remain stable. Rewritten descriptions and prospective approaches in Section 7 do not establish a new proposed algorithm, architecture, or implemented procedure.

E1.justification: The expanded multilingual, legal, mathematical, and long-context resources in Section 5 are catalogued for readers, without new training or evaluation on them. The original resource-profiling scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Figures 5, 7, and 8 retain their respective model comparison sets. The method tables summarize prior research; the revision does not add or remove methods in an experimental baseline comparison.

E3.justification: FLOPs profiling still measures a forward and backward pass with batch size 16, and memory profiling remains full-parameter fine-tuning. No substantive protocol revision is reported. The expanded benchmark and metric catalogue does not document newly executed evaluations.

E4.justification: The resource analyses and Figure 6's heterogeneity illustration are retained. Added descriptions of robustness and long-context benchmarks do not supply new ablations, sensitivity analyses, or robustness tests performed by this work.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars for the profiling measurements. Their uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: The original profiling values remain unchanged, including 51.85 and 98.56 GB in Figure 7. However, v2 Section 7 adds a literature-attributed estimate exceeding 50 GB for LoRA fine-tuning of LLaMA2-13B. This is additional reported resource evidence, not a new same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The transformer, LoRA, prompt-concatenation, and adapter mathematics remain equivalent. The prompt equation moves inline, and adapter variables and equation numbers change, without a substantive mathematical revision or new proof.

C1.justification: The central survey, taxonomy, and four-challenge claims persist. The abstract and third contribution recast the claimed novel evaluation benchmark as a review or framework of existing datasets and benchmarks across domains. The first-comprehensive-survey claim remains.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds substantive discussion of modality imbalance and alignment, continual adaptation and catastrophic forgetting, and PEFT's remaining memory limitations. It also develops security recommendations, substantially extending v1's outlook on model security and LLM–SLM collaboration.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds extensive dataset language, construction, and size information, alongside numerous direct data/source links. Conversely, v1's dedicated model-selection and lm-evaluation-harness guidance is removed. The project repository link is retained; these documentation changes do not establish altered experiments.

R1.justification: Literature coverage expands substantially through resources such as LongBench and LegalBench and discussions citing QLoRA, continual learning, and multimodal research. Table 1 adds application and future-direction comparisons. These are substantive additions beyond citation renumbering or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, background, and method explanations undergo extensive rewriting. Section 5 changes from traditional-NLP/instruction-task organization to separate domain-based dataset and benchmark inventories. The outlook is restructured, the conclusion becomes Section 8, and author information expands.

P2.justification: The document switches from two columns to one with wrapped illustrations. Figure 9 is redrawn as a compact taxonomy, v1 Tables 8–10 merge into v2 Table 8, Table 1 expands, and substantial new resource Tables 9–11 appear with very small text.

improvement.justification: v2 more accurately frames its benchmark contribution as a resource review and provides better organized dataset, metric, and access guidance. Its expanded discussion identifies specific deployment limitations. These benefits are tempered by removal of dedicated traditional-NLP, model-selection, and evaluation-tool guidance and the dense presentation of Tables 9–11, supporting a limited net improvement.
